entities.summary: Oreus or Oreos, prior to the 5th century BC called Histiaea or Histiaia (Ἱστίαια), also Hestiaea or Hestiaia (Ἑστίαια), was a town near the north coast of ancient Euboea, situated upon the river Callas, at the foot of Mount Telethrium, and opposite Antron on the Thessalian coast. From this town the whole northern extremity of Euboea was named Histiaeotis According to some it was a colony from the Attic deme of Histiaea; according to others it was founded by the Thessalian Perrhaebi. Another foundation story had it that the name Histiaea is said to derive from the mythical figure Histiaea, the daughter of Hyrieus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a major port and commercial center in ancient Euboea, Histiaea played a significant role in the regional trade networks of Southern Europe during the Classical era. Its strategic location facilitated the exchange of goods and ideas between Greece and other Mediterranean regions.
